thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — Sev2 / potential sensitive-data exposure detected by realtime-log-monitor. ID: INC-2026-0421 · channel: #incidents · triggered by alert rule `logs-scan:api-keys`

sophie (oncall): acked. i'm on it. paging raj + elaine. paging policy: 15m response expected. /ack (pagerduty)

pagerduty-bot: sophie (oncall) acknowledged the incident. Escalation to raj (eng-sre) in 4m.

raj (eng-sre): on my way. quick ask — do we know which envs are impacted? prod only or staging as well?

elaine (security): initial query shows log ingestion pipeline had a misapplied scrubbing rule between 03:40-04:15 UTC. suspected leaked tokens in application logs. running targeted search now to count distinct tokens and associated client IDs.

sophie (oncall): timeline noted. i'll start a live doc and call a short triage huddle in 10.

matt (ops): i'm isolating the ingestion shard that wrote the affected logs so we can stop further writes to long-term store. will update in +5

elaine (security): preliminary numbers: ~120 unique token-like strings surfaced, of which 18 match active API keys (rotated within 90d). likely scope: subset of Hosted API customers and some Dedicated test tenants. doing owner lookup now.

tom (legal): thx. we need to confirm PII exposure, and whether tokens grant access to customer data. if keys were active, we must prepare notification options and evaluate disclosure obligations under GDPR/CCPA. keep legal in the loop for drafts.

jess (product): we should prep status page language + a customer notice draft. aim to send targeted notifications only to affected customers after scope confirmed.

elaine (security): owner lookup: 12 distinct customer accounts map to active keys, 6 internal test accounts. for the 12 customers, i'm checking whether keys had recent activity (last 30d). initial: 9 had activity in last 7d.

raj (eng-sre): logs export of the 04:00-04:15 window is preserved. i pulled a copy for forensics. no evidence yet of exfil via our external endpoints. still investigating whether any requests used the leaked keys from outside our infra.

sophie (oncall): handoff — i'll stay through the next 45m then hand to raj for overnight. tagging @elaine and @tom for customer comm signoff.

elaine (security): draft notification below — please review, legal. this is written for email and portal DM. NOTE: we are keeping wording conservative, avoid overclaiming.

elaine (security): ```Subject: Important: Potential exposure of API credentials

Hello <Customer Name>,

We are contacting you about a potential exposure of API credentials that may affect a small subset of customers. On 2026-04-21 at ~04:00 UTC, a logging configuration change resulted in sensitive strings (including API credentials) being written to application logs for a limited time window (~35 minutes). We have identified a set of affected credentials and are still confirming the exact scope.

What we know so far:
- The logging misconfiguration affected logs written between 04:00 and 04:35 UTC on 2026-04-21.
- We have identified evidence of 12 customer credentials within that window; 9 of those credentials had request activity in the last 7 days.
- We have no evidence at this time that any third party accessed customer accounts using the exposed credentials. We are actively investigating for any unauthorized activity.

What we are doing:
- Immediately rotating all exposed credentials and issuing replacement keys for affected customers.
- Isolating and remediating the logging pipeline configuration to prevent recurrence.
- Conducting a full forensics review and retention of relevant logs.
- Offering assistance to rotate credentials and verify integration continuity.

Next steps:
- We will provide a follow-up within 48 hours with final scope and any recommended actions.
- If you believe you have observed suspicious activity, please contact our security team at security@redwood.example and include your account ID.

We apologize for the inconvenience and take this matter seriously. We are committed to transparency and prompt remediation.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Security Team
```

sophie (oncall): I'm adding a short status page blurb draft to be approved for posting to status.redwood.example:

elaine (security): status page draft (short): ```Incident: Potential exposure of API credentials — Partial service impact for a subset of customers. We identified a logging misconfiguration that temporarily wrote sensitive credential strings to logs between 04:00-04:35 UTC on 2026-04-21. Remediation in progress; affected customers are being contacted directly.``` Please keep it high level.

tom (legal): suggested edits to customer notice: remove speculative phrasing about 'no evidence' unless we can support it. prefer: "At this time we have not confirmed any unauthorized use; we are investigating." Also, add data residency line and regulatory contact: "If you require an escalation to your compliance contact, email compliance@redwood.example."

elaine (security): accepted, editing now. also adding CTA for customers to rotate keys if they prefer immediate mitigation.

jess (product): + add a short FAQ entry. customers will ask: "Do we need to rotate immediately?" Suggested answer: "We are rotating exposed keys proactively; we recommend you rotate any credentials you believe may be impacted and confirm integrations." Keep simple.

sophie (oncall): tagging the webhook owner — @matt — please ensure the statuspage publish has conservative visibility (public page + targeted email to affected customers only). we should not post the full list publicly.

matt (ops): will coordinate with statuspage team and suppress verbose details. publishing window 30m after legal signoff.

raj (eng-sre): quick mitigation notes for runbook: 1) revoke keys server-side 2) blacklist token fingerprints 3) rotate affected consumer keys and notify 4) search for external use patterns (abuse IPs etc)

elaine (security): forensics update in 20m. initial evidence suggests tokens were logged but we have zero hits from external IPs matched to those tokens in our request logs between 04:00-06:00 UTC. still scanning external threat intel feeds.

tom (legal): prepping notification matrix and regulatory triggers. likely customer notification required; breach-reporting thresholds under certain jurisdictions may apply depending on confirmed misuse or PII. will loop in CISO.

sophie (oncall): quick checklist before send: [x] scope-ish confirmed (12 customers) [x] mitigation path defined [ ] legal signoff [ ] status page approved [ ] customer email list finalized

elaine (security): legal signoff requested. draft updated per tom's edits, removing absolute claims. pushing final to #incidents in 8m.

tom (legal): signing off on wording now. final line tweak: add dedicated security contact and phone for enterprise customers. ok to proceed with targeted emails and statuspage publish.

jess (product): i've prepared the CSV of affected accounts for ops. sending via the secure channel now.

matt (ops): received CSV via vault message. scheduling staged email send at :30 past the hour. will include rotational tokens and instructions.

sophie (oncall): handing to raj for the overnight. i'll post a short handoff note at 1747607621 and remain reachable. thanks team.

raj (eng-sre): taking over. running final checks on revocation and rotation scripts. will update thread when done. please add any followups here.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — remediation steps executed: rotated 12 exposed credentials, isolated affected ingestion shard, retained forensic copies. Next update scheduled within 24h.

sophie (oncall): (reaction) :thumbsup:

elaine (security): follow-up tasks: 1) compile copy of all affected token fingerprints 2) correlate with downstream caches (CDN/KV) 3) ensure logs scrub policy is auto-tested in CI

tom (legal): please keep the audit trail of all communications. i'll prepare a short internal memo for executives summarizing scope, customer outreach, and regulatory posture.

raj (eng-sre): update: no external misuse detected in our traffic logs or public telemetry. continuing monitoring for 48h.

matt (ops): statuspage posted, targeted emails queued and sent. tracked sends show 9 customers acknowledged and started rotation.

elaine (security): final note: will produce official incident report (confidential) once forensics completes. expect full writeup in ~72h. if anything changes, i'll reopen this thread.

sophie (oncall): handing off complete. thread parked for oncall-to-oncall continuity. thanks all.
